To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified a transient cell population during the early neural differentiation of human embryonice stem cells (hESC), which expresses both the pluripotency marker Oct4 and the neuronal marker Pax6 and can give rise to both neural and non neural cell types.

the sequential loss of the surface antigens Tra-1- 81 and SSEA 4 during neural differentiation of hESCs identifies a transient cell population with the characteristics of an intermediate stage between pluripotent stem and neural progenitor cells.

the transient Tra-1−81(−)/ SSEA4(+) (T/S4+) cell population represents a distinct cell population that can give rise to both neural and nonneural cell types, depending on their extracellular environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the earliest differentiating cells during neural differentiation of human embryonal stem cells (hESC), the TR−/SSEA4+ cells.
the early differentiation of human ES cells into neural lineages.
the identification of early differentiating cells in neural differentiation of human embryionic stem cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the TR−/SSE4+ cell population represents an intermediate cell population between the undifferentiated hESC population and the committed neural progenitor cell population during early neural differentiation.

the TR-S4+ cell population identified in the early stage neural differentiation of human embryogenic stem cells (hESC), is distinct from both undiffentiated hESCs (hESC) and their committed neural precursor cells (NPCs).
the TR-S4+ cell population represents a transient population that exists in the early stages of neural differentiation of hESCs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a transient population of cells that are in between the pluripotent state and the neural lineage.
we identified a novel cell population in the neural differentiation of hESCs.
we have identified and characterized the early neural differentiation cells in hESCs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pluripotent factors Oct4 and Sox-2 play different roles in neural differentiation of hESCs.
the pluripotent factors Oct4 and Sox 2 play a different role in the neural differentiation of human embryotic stem cells (hESC).
the early differentiating cells in neural differentiation of hESCs are a distinct population that can be identified and isolated based on their expression of Tra-1‐81 and SSEA‐4.
